summary: Strengthen central bank policy, supervisory and operational decisions with practical casework and decision memos. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Central bank decision-making training focuses on institutional choices that shape conditions around corporate credit, not approval of individual borrowers. It is for policy, supervision and operations leaders who need to frame issues, evaluate evidence and make decisions traceable. Practical work uses Five Whys and decision trees to diagnose causes and compare options, then develops supervisory escalation rationales and decision memos with follow-up actions.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who make, prepare or review decisions across central bank policy, supervision and operations. It is designed for central bank leaders who need a repeatable way to evaluate evidence, align decision rights and record action.
modules: Central Bank Mandates and Decision Rights
Five Whys for Central Bank Diagnosis
Decision Trees for Central Bank Choices
Central Bank Decision Memos and Review
prerequisites: Working knowledge of central bank policy, supervision, financial stability or operations is expected. Practical exposure to preparing, reviewing or implementing institutional decisions will help you apply the exercises. No coding or programming is required.
